questions.stem:
The pie charts below show the distribution of students of graduate and post-graduate levels in seven different institutes in a town.

| Institute | Share of graduate students | Share of post-graduate students |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P | 12% | 12% |
| Q | 13% | 13% |
| R | 17% | 14% |
| S | 14% | 21% |
| T | 15% | 17% |
| M | 17% | 8% |
| N | 12% | 15% |

**Total number of students of graduate level = 27,300.**
**Total number of students of post-graduate level = 24,700.**

What is the total number of graduate and post-graduate level students in institute R?
questions.explanation:
Take R's share from each chart separately.

**Graduate:** $17\%$ of 27300
$$0.17 \times 27300 = 4641.$$

**Post-graduate:** $14\%$ of 24700
$$0.14 \times 24700 = 3458.$$

$$\text{Total} = 4641 + 3458 = \mathbf{8099}.$$

*(The two totals differ, so the percentages cannot simply be added — each must be applied to its own total.)*

**Total number of students of graduate level = 27,300.**
**Total number of students of post-graduate level = 24,700.**

What is the ratio between the number of students studying at post-graduate and graduate levels respectively in the institute S?
questions.explanation:
**Post-graduate:** $0.21 \times 24700 = 5187$.
**Graduate:** $0.14 \times 27300 = 3822$.

$$\frac{5187}{3822} = \frac{19}{14}$$
after dividing both by 273.

So the ratio is $\mathbf{19 : 14}$ — note the order asked for is post-graduate **first**, which is why $14:19$ is offered as a trap.

questions.stem:
The bar chart below shows the sale of cellular phones over six years.

| Year | 1997 | 1998 | 1999 | 2000 | 2001 | 2002 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cellular phones sold | 48000 | 40000 | 30000 | 25000 | 18000 | 40000 |

The difference in the sales of cellular phones for the years 1997 and 1999 is?
questions.explanation:
Read the two bars and subtract:
$$48000 - 30000 = \mathbf{18{,}000} \text{ units}.$$

questions.stem:
The bar chart below shows the sale of cellular phones over six years.

| Year | 1997 | 1998 | 1999 | 2000 | 2001 | 2002 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cellular phones sold | 48000 | 40000 | 30000 | 25000 | 18000 | 40000 |

The sum of sales of cellular phones in the years 1999 and 2001 is equal to that of which year?
questions.explanation:
$$1999 + 2001 = 30000 + 18000 = 48000.$$

Scanning the chart, 48000 is the figure for **1997**.

*(1998 and 2002 stand at 40000 and 2000 at 25000, so none of them matches.)*

questions.stem:
The bar chart below shows the sale of cellular phones over six years.

| Year | 1997 | 1998 | 1999 | 2000 | 2001 | 2002 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cellular phones sold | 48000 | 40000 | 30000 | 25000 | 18000 | 40000 |

The percentage increase in sales from 2001 to 2002 was?
questions.explanation:
The increase is measured against the **earlier** year, 2001:
$$\frac{40000 - 18000}{18000} \times 100 = \frac{22000}{18000} \times 100 = 122.2\%,$$

which rounds to **122%**.

*(Dividing by 2002's figure instead would give 55% — the usual error in percentage-change questions.)*

questions.stem:
The line graph below shows the **ratio of exports to imports** of two companies A and B over the years 1995 to 2000.

| Year | 1995 | 1996 | 1997 | 1998 | 1999 | 2000 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Company A | 1.75 | 1.5 | 1.75 | 0.75 | 0.75 | 1.0 |
| Company B | 0.75 | 0.75 | 1.0 | 1.25 | 1.0 | 1.25 |

In how many of the given years were the exports more than the imports for Company A?
questions.explanation:
Exports exceed imports exactly when the ratio is **greater than 1**.

Company A's ratios are $1.75, 1.5, 1.75, 0.75, 0.75, 1.0$, so the years above 1 are
$$1995 \;(1.75), \quad 1996 \;(1.5), \quad 1997 \;(1.75) \;-\; \mathbf{3 \text{ years}}.$$

*(2000 has a ratio of exactly 1, meaning exports **equal** imports, so it does not count.)*

questions.stem:
The line graph below shows the **ratio of exports to imports** of two companies A and B over the years 1995 to 2000.

| Year | 1995 | 1996 | 1997 | 1998 | 1999 | 2000 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Company A | 1.75 | 1.5 | 1.75 | 0.75 | 0.75 | 1.0 |
| Company B | 0.75 | 0.75 | 1.0 | 1.25 | 1.0 | 1.25 |

If the exports of Company A in 1998 were ₹237 crores, what was the amount of imports in that year?
questions.explanation:
The graph gives a ratio, not an amount:
$$\frac{\text{Exports}}{\text{Imports}} = 0.75 \text{ in 1998 for Company A}.$$

So
$$\text{Imports} = \frac{237}{0.75} = \mathbf{₹316 \text{ crores}}.$$

*(Multiplying instead of dividing would give ₹177.75 crores — the ratio being below 1 means imports must be the **larger** figure.)*

questions.stem:
The line graph below shows the **ratio of exports to imports** of two companies A and B over the years 1995 to 2000.

| Year | 1995 | 1996 | 1997 | 1998 | 1999 | 2000 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Company A | 1.75 | 1.5 | 1.75 | 0.75 | 0.75 | 1.0 |
| Company B | 0.75 | 0.75 | 1.0 | 1.25 | 1.0 | 1.25 |

In how many years were the imports more than the exports for company 'B'?
questions.explanation:
Imports exceed exports when the ratio is **less than 1**.

Company B's ratios are $0.75, 0.75, 1.0, 1.25, 1.0, 1.25$, so the years below 1 are
$$1995 \text{ and } 1996 \;-\; \mathbf{2 \text{ years}}.$$

*(1997 and 1999 sit exactly at 1 — equal, not more.)*
